claims.explanation: NVP-AUY922 is a potent HSP90 inhibitor whose selectivity is largely driven by dependence on HSP90 client proteins, especially oncogenic kinases and steroid receptors that are stabilized by the HSP90 chaperone. Lines with high expression or amplification of HSP90 clients such as ERBB2, ERBB3, MET, CDK4/6, and mutant BRAF or EGFR are therefore expected to be sensitized, while features that buffer proteotoxic stress or reduce drug exposure (e.g., high HSPA1A/HSPA1B, NQO1, or ABCB1) may be protective. The transcriptional signature (HSP72/BAG3 induction, MYC and EZH2 depletion) confirms on-target HSP90 inhibition.

features.basis: ERBB2 is a classic HSP90 client; HER2-amplified breast lines are among the most sensitive (PMID 18430202, 18413753)
ERBB3 is an HSP90 client and was induced in the virtual cell signature; high expression predicts dependence
Mutant BRAF is an HSP90 client and BRAF-mutant melanoma lines are sensitive to HSP90 inhibition
Mutant EGFR is an HSP90 client; EGFR-driven lung cancers show sensitivity to HSP90 inhibitors
MET is an HSP90 client kinase; amplification/overexpression predicts sensitivity
CDK4 is an HSP90 client; high expression or amplification increases dependence
Cyclin D1 is an HSP90 client; amplification/overexpression predicts sensitivity
Estrogen receptor is an HSP90 client; ER-positive breast cancer lines are sensitive
High HSP70 buffers HSP90 inhibition and correlates with resistance (PMID 23065523)
HSP70 family members functionally compensate for HSP90 inhibition (PMID 23065523)
NQO1 expression does not affect NVP-AUY922 activity, but high levels may alter redox balance and drug response
Efflux pump overexpression can reduce intracellular drug levels and confer resistance
